facts.fact: Phil walks the moor road towards Wroxborough in fog and rain, and her phone starts downloading texts once she is past the school's signal-null area.
facts.anchor: She must have emerged from the weird null area in which the school lay.

facts.fact: At a crossroads that should not exist, Phil sees Margot Hamilton standing under a street lamp with a stranger, later named Anne Bredon.
facts.anchor: one of them was Margot Hamilton. The other was a stranger.

facts.fact: Anne Bredon tells Phil she wants her to break the wards, suggesting midnight as the time.
facts.anchor: I want you to break the wards.

facts.fact: Anne sends Margot back along the road to school before stating her business, so the girl will not overhear.
facts.anchor: watched the small figure slouch along the road back towards school.

facts.fact: Phil refuses Anne's offer of money, citing her duty of care to the pupils.
facts.anchor: I do have a duty of care

facts.fact: Phil walks away; when she turns back, Anne Bredon, her mouse and the crossroads are all gone.
facts.anchor: the road swept on to the horizon, serene and uncrossed by any other highway.

facts.fact: A flaming leopard-like creature charges Phil, recoils when she throws up her hands, and speaks before vanishing.
facts.anchor: Tell him that his seal will not protect you next time.

facts.fact: Phil backs away step by step past the gorse thicket, the creature stops following, and she heads back to the school.
facts.anchor: She stumbled backwards, past the bushes

facts.fact: Anne Bredon is the Latin mistress whose post Phil now holds - Phil's predecessor.
facts.anchor: the people who try to fill your shoes

facts.fact: Margot Hamilton is a pupil at the school and a former Latin pupil of Anne Bredon.
facts.anchor: looking forward to having you teaching us again, Miss

facts.fact: Jane Worth is the school's maths teacher and had refused to drive Phil into Wroxborough.
facts.anchor: Maths teacher, somewhat prickly, not very enthusiastic about teaching

facts.fact: Margot is an adolescent schoolgirl living under the Head's (Miss Jagerson's) authority.
facts.anchor: Miss Jagerson will have taken precautions.

facts.fact: Anne Bredon is described as about ten years older than Phil and half a foot taller.
facts.anchor: looked about ten years older than Phil, and half a foot taller

facts.fact: The night is in November; Anne sets the task at midnight, any midnight.
facts.anchor: Midnight would be good. Any midnight.

facts.fact: Phil has walked twenty minutes and expects at least another half-hour to Wroxborough's outskirts.
facts.anchor: Phil had been walking for twenty minutes or so now
